dialect.detail: Likely compiled with a PC-based COBOL compiler (GnuCOBOL or Micro Focus) given Windows-style relative paths and ASSIGN TO PRINTER; student assignment context. PROGRAM-ID and AUTHOR use quoted strings without period, which is non-standard syntax.
evidence: OCCURS 1 TO 50 TIMES DEPENDING ON (ODO - COBOL-85)

purpose.domain_detail: Student assignment for a college COBOL course; processes student test scores against a subject file and produces a grade tally report
purpose.summary: This program reads a student data file and a subject file, populates an ODO table of subjects, then for each student record finds the matching subject and tallies grades (A through F) per subject. It prints a summary report of grade counts by subject plus totals.

notable_features: OCCURS DEPENDING ON (ODO table) for variable-length subject table
EVALUATE TRUE with range conditions for grade classification
ASSIGN TO PRINTER for print output
Windows-style relative file paths in ASSIGN clauses
Non-standard PROGRAM-ID and AUTHOR syntax (quoted strings without period)
Missing OPEN of F02-SUBJECT-FILE under correct name (bug: opens F01-SUBJECT-FILE instead)
W02-TOTALS group item missing period after level-01 (syntax issue)
verdict.notes: The code contains several apparent bugs/syntax issues consistent with a student exercise: PROGRAM-ID uses quoted string without period; W02-TOTALS 01-level entry is missing a period; the 100-OPEN-FILES paragraph opens F01-SUBJECT-FILE instead of F02-SUBJECT-FILE; W02-A-COUNT referenced but defined as W02-A-TOTAL in the group. The 'bbb' and 'yyyy/mm/dd' placeholders in DISPLAY statements confirm incomplete/draft status.
